summary: Source Workbench administrative Job/Result Save and Delete require matching verified collection and draft source identities with a current effective API authority. Missing, stale, mismatched or unreadable source checks block before backend work; the GUI disables the four writes and offers explicit read-only refresh with translated draft-replacement guidance for four built-in and thirty catalogued languages. Same-source reads retain dirty editing; verified new-source reads replace prior-source fields even when record IDs match. Weak metadata attaches once per collection and deletion filters retain its original source without retagging; serialized payloads and public schemas remain unchanged. Source-client mocked Chromium controls and pure frontend controls verify this bounded behavior. This is not backend authorization, authenticated provenance, cross-client locking, continuous authority-history fencing, installed WebView, remote deployment, power-loss, cold-start storage-fault or scientific qualification. No persistent snapshot, archive, backup, write replay, production Node dependency or operational-grade promotion is introduced.

required_text: an old record or draft must not authorize a write on the new backend
a copied collection is not automatically verified
source-preserving deletion filters never retag an old collection as the current backend
unreadable record-source checks fail closed without throwing through UI rendering
is safe to display but blocks HTTP without selecting a fallback
